questions.q: How does the summary distinguish pleasure from enjoyment?
a: Pleasure is sensory and pulls attention away, while enjoyment is focused
Pleasure lasts longer, while enjoyment fades quickly
Pleasure comes from effort, while enjoyment comes from rest
Pleasure is learned, while enjoyment is purely genetic
questions.why: Lesson 1 says enjoyment returns control of your attention and leads to real happiness.

When the task is far easier than your abilities
When a reward is promised for finishing quickly
When you work alone without any distractions
questions.why: Lesson 2 says flow sits between frustration and boredom.

questions.q: What happens when a challenge is too hard or too easy?
a: You become frustrated or bored and lose the flow
You enter flow more quickly because of the contrast
You retain more of what you learn in the session
You naturally increase your skill within minutes
questions.why: Lesson 2 places flow between the two failure modes of anxiety and boredom.

questions.q: What kind of activity is most likely to trigger flow?
a: One you find meaningful and do without money or fame as a motive
One that pays well and offers clear public recognition
One that is completely new and has no rules at all
One that you can finish in a single sitting
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the activity should be rewarding in itself, with no external incentive.

questions.q: What does the summary say about setting a life goal?
a: Any goal works if it keeps you in flow and keeps growing harder
Only a goal that helps others is worth committing to
A life goal should be chosen before you turn thirty
Goals matter less than enjoying each day as it comes
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the content matters less than whether the goal sustains flow.
